verdict.rationale: Keycloak's docs cover defining and enforcing roles and permissions. It offers role-based authorization, and its Authorization Services add fine-grained, resource-level permissions with role-based and JS policies, managed from the admin console, kcadm, or the Admin REST API. Policies are evaluated via UMA permission tickets, and tokens can be checked through the introspection endpoint. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that role and permission claims are embedded in access/ID tokens, and independent hands-on corroboration of token-based authorization checks.
